text:
incident-bot: Pager triggered -> HIGH 5xx rate during rolling release v3.2.1 in eu-west-1 for service=inference-api. Affected target group=prod-inference. Alert: 5xx > 10% over 5m, spike to 18%. Runbook: https://internal/runbooks/inference/queue-saturation
PagerDuty: Page PD-2026-84721 fired (severity: P1). Notifying on-call rotation.
Jamie (oncall): ack - I'm taking this. @Alex K @Maria P @Suresh R can you jump in?
Alex K: looking at access logs — nginx upstream reset + 503s from inference-worker pods. Error rate correlates with rollout pods of v3.2.1. Flux of queued requests piling up at queue-proxy.
Maria P: I paused the rollout in the cluster: `kubectl rollout pause deployment/inference-api -n prod` — verifying current replica set pinned.
Suresh R: adding capacity to queue-proxy to mitigate backlog: `kubectl scale deployment/queue-proxy -n prod --replicas=6` — scaling now.
PagerDuty: Acknowledged by Jamie (oncall).
Jamie (oncall): Good. Support — what is customer impact?
Support Rep: Support ticket #6789 opened; several EU customers reporting 503s during request spikes (~20% of active sessions in eu-west-1). No billing impact reported, but user-facing failures.
Alex K: I can see request batching/prefetch feature introduced in v3.2.1 touching the queue layer. Suspect head-of-line blocking when small-batch requests intermix with large-batch. Also seeing GC churn in a subset of worker pods.
Maria P: We should rollback release to v3.2.0 while we triage. I'm prepared to execute rollback when we decide.
Jamie (oncall): Agree. Initiating immediate rollback to v3.2.0. Triggering through deploy bot.
Alex K: Deploy bot logs: ```deploy-bot: rolling back inference-api from v3.2.1 -> v3.2.0```
Alex K: kubectl command used: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/inference-api -n prod --to-revision=202`
Maria P: Rollback started. Watching health checks.
incident-bot: Monitoring events: older RS scaled up, new RS scaled down. Healthcheck fail count decreasing.
Suresh R: After rollback, error rate dropped from 18% -> 1.2% over 10m. Latency back to baseline (p50 85ms, p95 420ms -> baseline p95 ~300ms).
Support Rep: Confirming reduced customer reports. Updating ticket #6789: rollback executed, customers notified.
Jamie (oncall): Great. Creating incident ticket and assigning to eng-runtime for postmortem. I'm handing off to Suresh for post-incident follow-ups and RCA in 30m.
Suresh R: I'll own the postmortem. Immediate next steps: collect heap/GC traces from affected pods, capture queue-proxy metrics, reproduce locally with staging workload.
Alex K: For mitigation checklist: (1) keep rollout paused, (2) add a canary traffic limit for batching change, (3) revert prefetch flag by default until patch validated, (4) add early-failback to fallback model variant on high queue latency.
Maria P: Noted. I'll leave rollout paused and set a deployment hold in the console.
PagerDuty: Closing alert PD-2026-84721 (status: resolved by ack & rollback).
Jamie (oncall): Thanks all. Quick post-incident note: severity P1 due to customer-visible errors; rollback restored service. We'll meet for a blameless postmortem to decide fix and safer rollout guards. cc @eng-runtime @devex
incident-bot: Incident logged: INC-2026-1254 (severity P1) — assigned to eng-runtime. SLA window captured.
Suresh R: Handoff to me now — I'll collect logs and link artifacts in the incident ticket within 30m.
Alex K: Attaching a short sample log snippet for the ticket: ```[nginx] upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client=10.7.2.44, server=inference-api, request="POST /v1/generate"```
Maria P: All service checks green. I'll keep monitoring for 20m then unpause only with a tightly controlled canary.
Jamie (oncall): Closing channel updates here; will post summary to #postmortems and calendar invite for RCA tomorrow. Thanks team :thumbsup:
